- **Horse warfare (chariot, cavalry, horse archers)** [`cavalry_chariot`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cavalry_chariot.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Imperial cuirassiers, dragoons and Croats face Ottoman sipahis and Tatar light horse, who devastate Lower Austria. The Polish winged hussars charge with lances on 12 September. Local: Duke Charles of Lorraine's cavalry north of the Danube.
- **Bows of war (composite bow, crossbow, longbow)** [`crossbow_longbow`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/crossbow_longbow.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept low. European armies have given up bows; crossbows survive in shooting clubs. Tatars and Ottoman horsemen still use the composite bow, and arrows fall in the city.
- **Mechanical artillery (torsion catapult, trebuchet)** [`torsion_artillery_trebuchet`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/torsion_artillery_trebuchet.md) — K2, use none, make medium, accept low. Known from Vegetius and Lipsius as antiquities. Mortars throwing bombs and stones do this work on both sides.
- **Oared war galley and ram tactics** [`oared_galley_ram`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/oared_galley_ram.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. On the Danube both sides use armed oared boats (Tschaiken). The Ottomans control the river arms at Vienna and bridge them. Galleys are Venice's and the Sultan's business. Local: Tschaikisten boatmen of Komorn and Raab. Elsewhere: Venice: Arsenal and galley fleet.
- **Incendiary weapons and Greek fire** [`incendiaries_greek_fire`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/incendiaries_greek_fire.md) — K3, use correct, make easy, accept high. Fireworkers make pitch wreaths, fire-balls, storm barrels and hand grenades to defend ditch and breach. Ottoman bombs and fire-arrows threaten roofs. 'Greek fire' is a legend. Local: arsenal fireworkers (Feuerwerker); pitch, sulphur and saltpetre stocks.
- **Field fortification (marching camp, wagon fort, entrenchment)** [`field_fortification`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/field_fortification.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Ottoman sappers dig covered approach trenches faster than any western army. Kara Mustafa leaves his camp without lines against a relief army, which decides the battle of 12 September.
- **Gunpowder (black powder)** [`gunpowder`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/gunpowder.md) — K4, use correct, make medium, accept high. The garrison fights on stored powder; a fire at the Schottenstift on 14 July nearly reaches the magazine. Saltpetre is the limit. Local: imperial arsenal near the Schottenstift; saltpetre boilers; apothecaries (sulphur).
- **Cannon and artillery** [`cannon_artillery`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/cannon_artillery.md) — K4, use correct, make medium, accept high. The walls carry bronze and iron pieces from the imperial and civic arsenals, 130 to 300 by different counts. The Ottomans bring mostly light guns and rely on mines. Local: Kaiserliches Zeughaus; Bürgerliches Zeughaus Am Hof; bell and gun founders.
- **Ballistics and scientific gunnery** [`ballistics_gunnery`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/ballistics_gunnery.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Gunners lay by quadrant, rules of thumb and trial shots. Galileo's parabola is in books; no one corrects for air. Mortar fire with fused bombs is the specialists' art. Local: Büchsenmeister and Feuerwerker of the arsenal; Michael Mieth (imperial artillery officer, Artilleriae recentior praxis, 1683). Elsewhere: Paris: Blondel, L'art de jetter les bombes (1683); England: Robert Anderson (1674).
- **Handguns and muskets (matchlock, flintlock)** [`handguns_muskets`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/handguns_muskets.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. The matchlock musket is the standard arm; flintlocks are spreading with dragoons, grenadiers and hunters. Janissary muskets are long, heavy and accurate. Local: gunsmiths of Vienna and Wiener Neustadt; civic arsenal Am Hof. Elsewhere: Suhl, Ferlach, Brescia: gun-making centres.
- **Pike and shot, volley fire and drill** [`pike_and_shot_drill`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pike_and_shot_drill.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Imperial battalions mix pikes with a growing majority of muskets and fire by ranks, following Montecuccoli. Against Turkish horse they carry portable spiked barriers. Local: Montecuccoli's regulations and writings (he died in 1680).
- **Socket bayonet** [`socket_bayonet`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/socket_bayonet.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Plug bayonets pushed into the muzzle are known from French troops; they stop the musket firing. A blade on a sleeve round the barrel is unknown here. Pikes remain. Local: Vienna cutlers and gunsmiths. Elsewhere: France: plug bayonets issued since 1671; Vauban's socket design adopted 1688–89.
- **Bastioned fortification (trace italienne)** [`bastion_fortification`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bastion_fortification.md) — K4, use partial, make hard, accept high. Bastions were built from the 1540s after the siege of 1529; ravelins were finished by 1672. By 1682 they were neglected: weak counterscarp, no countermines at the Burg bastion. Local: Georg Rimpler (chief engineer since 1682); Daniel Suttinger; Burgbastei, Löwelbastei and the Burg ravelin; Count Ernst Rüdiger von Starhemberg. Elsewhere: France: Vauban's fortresses (Lille, Strasbourg from 1681); Dutch Republic: Menno van Coehoorn.
- **Siegecraft, mining and counter-mining** [`siegecraft_mining`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/siegecraft_mining.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Ottoman miners, practised at Candia (1648–1669), are the best in Europe. The city has few; Rimpler recruits some from Tyrol, the Netherlands and Lorraine. Listeners watch water tubs for ripples. Local: Georg Rimpler (wounded 25 July, dies 2–3 August); cellars along the Löwelbastei as listening posts; miners recruited from Tyrol and Lorraine. Elsewhere: France: Vauban's parallels (Maastricht 1673); Ottoman lagımcı miner corps.
- **Broadside gunnery and the line of battle** [`naval_gunnery_line_of_battle`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/naval_gunnery_line_of_battle.md) — K2, use none, make impossible, accept low. Fireworkers make rockets for court festivals and signals; Siemienowicz's artillery book (1650, German 1676) is their manual. As a weapon they are thought too inaccurate. Local: arsenal Feuerwerker; signal rockets from St Stephen's tower.
- **Standing army, pay and supply** [`standing_army_logistics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/standing_army_logistics.md) — K3, use partial, make hard, accept medium. The emperor has kept permanent regiments since 1649, run by the Hofkriegsrat. Pay is months in arrears; supply depends on contractors and on what the estates vote. Local: Hofkriegsrat (president Margrave Hermann of Baden); Generalkriegskommissariat; Samuel Oppenheimer (army contractor). Elsewhere: France: Louvois' magazines and intendants.
- **Mercenaries, militias and the loyalty of armed men** [`mercenaries_citizen_militia`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/mercenaries_citizen_militia.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. About 11,000 regular troops enter on 10–13 July. About 5,000 citizens and volunteers join them: eight burgher companies under the mayor, students, court servants, merchants and guild companies. Local: Mayor Johann Andreas von Liebenberg (colonel of the citizen militia); university companies (Paul de Sorbait); Stadtguardia.
- **Conscription and the mass army** [`conscription_mass_army`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/conscription_mass_army.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept low. The estates can call up every thirtieth or tenth man for local defence, poorly armed. Regiments recruit by bounty. On 26 August every man in the city is called up.
- **Camp hygiene and army health** [`military_camp_hygiene`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/military_camp_hygiene.md) — K2, use none, make easy, accept medium. 'Red dysentery' spreads from early August; Starhemberg is ill 11–20 August. Rubbish, carcasses and shallow graves are blamed for bad air; wells and latrines are not suspected. Local: Bürgerspital and convent hospitals; Bishop Kollonitsch; Paul de Sorbait.

The emperor has no engineer corps; engineers are hired foreigners, labour is pressed peasants and townspeople. The relief army crosses the Danube on boat bridges at Tulln. Montecuccoli, victor of St Gotthard (1664), wrote the leading treatises on war against the Turks; they circulate in manuscript among officers. Vegetius and Lipsius are school authors. Local: Charles of Lorraine; Hofkriegsrat.

The Hofkriegsrat (1556) is a slow administrative council. Command goes by rank and birth; plans are made in councils of war, as at Stetteldorf on 4 September.

Officers play chess; Weickhmann's enlarged 'king's game' (Ulm, 1664) is a curiosity. Counting shots, losses or mine results to choose tactics is not done.
- **Military intelligence and codebreaking** [`military_intelligence_codebreaking`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/military_intelligence_codebreaking.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Couriers in Turkish dress cross the lines (Kolschitzky, 13–17 August; Michaelowitz). Dispatches are ciphered with simple substitution and code lists. Both sides question prisoners and deserters. The frontier fortresses (Raab, Komorn) and the Vasvár peace were meant to hold the Porte. In 1683 the Ottomans bypass Raab and march straight on Vienna.
